title: Carbon pricing and corporate strategy
abstract: We study how firms adjust investment and pricing strategies in response to carbon taxes. Using emissions and financial data from industrial companies, we show that firms with higher energy intensity reduce capital spending, while others invest in cleaner technology to protect market share. Policy uncertainty weakens the effect. The results speak to managers, regulators and the economics of climate mitigation across supply chains and industries.

title: Public attitudes toward gene editing
abstract: Gene editing technologies raise ethical questions about safety, consent and equity. We surveyed citizens in several countries about their views on the use of genome engineering in agriculture and medicine. Respondents with higher science literacy expressed more support, while religious and political beliefs predicted opposition. The study discusses how communication and regulation can shape public trust in biotechnology.
